objectives: Use equations with more than three quantities

questions.q: Give the unit of specific heat capacity.

engage.hook: Which stores more energy: a brick on a shelf or a cup of hot tea?

questions.q: A 2 kg book is lifted 1.5 m. g = 9.8 N/kg. Find E_p.
A 60 kg climber gains 5880 J. g = 9.8 N/kg. Find h.
v = 20 m/s, u = 5 m/s, t = 3 s. Find a.

statements.text: Lifting twice as high halves the energy.
statements.correction: Twice as high stores twice the energy.

statements.text: Water heats up faster than oil.
statements.correction: Oil heats faster: lower specific heat capacity.

statements.text: A heavier block is always denser.
statements.correction: Density depends on mass and volume.

statements.text: g is the same everywhere in space.
statements.correction: g depends on the planet or moon.

graphNotes: Levels off when a reactant runs out.

developing.q: Write the equation for gravitational potential energy.
Name the quantity measured in J/kg°C.

reaching.q: A 3 kg mass is lifted 2 m. g = 9.8 N/kg. Find E_p.
Find the energy to heat 2 kg of water by 5°C. c = 4200 J/kg°C.
A block is 0.1 m by 0.1 m by 0.1 m with density 1000 kg/m^3. Find its mass.

mastering.q: Rearrange E_p = mgh to make h the subject.
Explain why a formula triangle cannot be used for a = (v - u)/t.
mastering.a: It is not one quantity equal to a product of the others

mastering.q: Find the temperature rise when 21000 J heats 1 kg of water. c = 4200 J/kg°C.
